title: What Guitar Slim was like
summary: Slim was funny, religious, generous with his car, wild about women, and was overcharged for a party in Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I was wondering, so a lot of these dates you went out with guitar slim. What kind of guy was slim?
Slim was a very humorous fellow man. He was a religious person believe it or not.

Yeah he believed in the Bible and he could recite the 23rd Psalms. And man he said like this and he told me he said, Mr. Cotton you and your wife y'all gonna outlive me. You gonna outlive me. You want my car? Because you know he couldn't trust everybody with their cars you know. I was always trust with it. He would let me have the car. Hose would always let me have the car. Anytime they got brought a brand new car I would be the first one to drive it. And I'd go pick the guys up in the city to bring them back to Tibeto to play out there when Slim lived out there in Tibeto with Hose. And anywhere we'd go. Slim would see my wife and I walking and he'd say, hey Cotton you wanna borrow my car? I said no man we're gonna walk you know. He always offered the car to us. There were times when he'd be down on his money.
Mitch Cotton can I borrow 50 dollars? She'd say yeah Slim sure.
I'll give you extra money. She'd say no just give me my 50 dollars back that's all. Whatever you borrow just give it back. We never try to get over on it.
Well it seems like he really trusted you.
It seems like there was a wilder side to him though.

He was very very wild. Than what you described. He was very very wild. But I mean he was a religious person a lot of people didn't really know him for what he really is. But he was crazy about women. He was crazy about women. So I mean he'd pick up a lady and every town he'd go. Whatever you had on you'd go with him and that was it. When you get to the next town he'd put you on the side and get the next woman. Now you either put up with that or you went back. You got on the best way you could. But that's one thing I knew about him. Now they set him up in Los Angeles because he was supposed to buy some uniforms. In Los Angeles they brought him to a party and he ended up paying two thousand dollars for the party. They say it was in his honor but they gave him the bill. The guy being the kind of guy he is he just went on to pay it. So we never get our uniform. We ended up in some parts of Ohio I forgot what it was. We used to play there all the time. Dayton, Ohio. We went to Dayton and we went downtown. That's the first time I bought a real heavy winter suit up there in Dayton. Because you know down here it doesn't really get cold. But up there man you need some bully willies up there. I've been there. Yes. Yes. So my brother-in-law, my wife brother he tried to get us to reside in Chicago. I said man it's too cold up here. I don't want to live up here. He was a barber. He could have got his sister to become a barber. I could have been a streetcar driver or anything I wanted to be man. I said no it's too cold up here. So we never, it was, I never did like up north. Not for a living. I could go visit.
